sanskrit: līnaṃ tu tasya gātreṣu mārjārasyātha mūṣakam tau dṛṣṭvā nakulolūkau nirāśau jagmatur gṛhān
english: But seeing the mouse clinging to the cat's body, the mongoose and the owl, their hopes dashed, went off to their lairs.

sanskrit: līnas tu tasya gātreṣu palito deśakālavit ciccheda pāśān nṛpate kālākāṅkṣī śanaiḥ śanaiḥ
english: Clinging to the cat's body, the grey-furred one, knowing place and time and awaiting the right moment, began to gnaw through the snares, O king, slowly, ever so slowly.

sanskrit: atha bandhaparikliṣṭo mārjāro vīkṣya mūṣakam chindantaṃ vai tadā pāśān atvarantaṃ tvarānvitaḥ
english: Then the cat, tormented by his bonds, watching the mouse cutting away at the snares without haste, grew anxious and impatient.

sanskrit: tam atvarantaṃ palitaṃ pāśānāṃ chedane tadā saṃcodayitum ārebhe mārjāro mūṣakaṃ tadā
english: And so the cat began to urge on the grey one, the mouse, who was taking his time in cutting through the snares.

sanskrit: kiṃ saumya nābhitvarase kiṃ kṛtārtho 'vamanyase chindhi pāśān amitraghna purā śvapaca eti saḥ
english: "Why, good friend, do you not hasten? Now that your end is gained, do you make light of me? Cut the snares, O slayer of foes, before the dog-cooking outcast comes!"

sanskrit: ity uktas tvaratā tena matimān palito 'bravīt mārjāram akṛtaprajñaṃ vaśyam ātmahitaṃ vacaḥ
english: Thus pressed to hurry by that one, the wise grey mouse spoke to the cat, whose understanding had not ripened—words measured and serving his own good:

sanskrit: tūṣṇīṃ bhava na te saumya tvarā kāryā na saṃbhramaḥ vayam evātra kālajñā na kālaḥ parihāsyate
english: "Be still, good friend; you need not rush, you need not be flustered. It is I here who know the moment, and the right moment shall not be let slip.

sanskrit: akāle kṛtyam ārabdhaṃ kartuṃ nārthāya kalpate tad eva kāla ārabdhaṃ mahate 'rthāya kalpate
english: A deed begun out of season serves no purpose when done; that very deed begun in season serves a great purpose.

sanskrit: akālavipramuktān me tvatta eva bhayaṃ bhavet tasmāt kālaṃ pratīkṣasva kim iti tvarase sakhe
english: Were I to free you out of season, from you alone would danger come to me. Therefore wait for the moment—why do you hurry so, my friend?

sanskrit: yāvat paśyāmi caṇḍālam āyāntaṃ śastrapāṇinam tataś chetsyāmi te pāśaṃ prāpte sādhāraṇe bhaye
english: When I see the outcast approaching, weapon in hand, then—the danger now being common to us both—I will cut your snare.

sanskrit: tasmin kāle pramuktas tvaṃ tarum evādhirohasi na hi te jīvitād anyat kiṃ cit kṛtyaṃ bhaviṣyati
english: Freed at that instant, you will climb straight up the tree; for then you will have no concern at all save saving your life.

sanskrit: tato bhavaty atikrānte traste bhīte ca lomaśa ahaṃ bilaṃ pravekṣyāmi bhavāñ śākhāṃ gamiṣyati
english: Then, once you have fled away, terrified and frightened, O shaggy one, I shall slip into my burrow while you make for a branch.

sanskrit: evam uktas tu mārjāro mūṣakeṇātmano hitam vacanaṃ vākyatattvajño jīvitārthī mahāmatiḥ
english: Thus addressed by the mouse with words serving his own good, the cat—shrewd, well-versed in the meaning of speech, and clinging to life—replied:

sanskrit: athātmakṛtyatvaritaḥ samyak praśrayam ācaran uvāca lomaśo vākyaṃ mūṣakaṃ cirakāriṇam
english: Pressed by his own need, the shaggy one, behaving now with all due deference, spoke to the slow-acting mouse:

sanskrit: na hy evaṃ mitrakāryāṇi prītyā kurvanti sādhavaḥ yathā tvaṃ mokṣitaḥ kṛcchrāt tvaramāṇena vai mayā
english: "This is not how the good do a friend's work out of affection—not the way I, in my haste, delivered you from peril.

sanskrit: tathaiva tvaramāṇena tvayā kāryaṃ hitaṃ mama yatnaṃ kuru mahāprājña yathā svasty āvayor bhavet
english: In that same haste you should do me good in turn. Make the effort, O most wise one, that all may be well with us both.

sanskrit: atha vā pūrvavairaṃ tvaṃ smaran kālaṃ vikarṣasi paśya duṣkṛtakarmatvaṃ vyaktam āyuḥkṣayo mama
english: Or is it that, remembering our old enmity, you are dragging out the time? Consider how wrongful such conduct would be: plainly, my life would be cut short.

sanskrit: yac ca kiṃ cin mayājñānāt purastād vipriyaṃ kṛtam na tan manasi kartavyaṃ kṣamaye tvāṃ prasīda me
english: Whatever offense I once did you in my ignorance, that you should not hold in your heart. I beg your pardon—be gracious to me."

sanskrit: tam evaṃvādinaṃ prājñaḥ śāstravid buddhisaṃmataḥ uvācedaṃ vacaḥ śreṣṭhaṃ mārjāraṃ mūṣakas tadā
english: To the cat speaking thus, the mouse—wise, learned in the treatises, and esteemed for his intelligence—then spoke these excellent words:

sanskrit: śrutaṃ me tava mārjāra svam arthaṃ parigṛhṇataḥ mamāpi tvaṃ vijānīhi svam arthaṃ parigṛhṇataḥ
english: "I have heard you, O cat, looking to your own interest; now understand me too, looking to mine.

sanskrit: yan mitraṃ bhītavat sādhyaṃ yan mitraṃ bhayasaṃhitam surakṣitaṃ tataḥ kāryaṃ pāṇiḥ sarpamukhād iva
english: A friend to be won over as though one were afraid, a friend bound up with danger—from such a one the hand must be well guarded, as from a serpent's mouth.

sanskrit: kṛtvā balavatā saṃdhim ātmānaṃ yo na rakṣati apathyam iva tad bhuktaṃ tasyānarthāya kalpate
english: He who, having made a pact with a stronger power, does not guard himself—that pact, like unwholesome food eaten, turns to his ruin.

sanskrit: na kaś cit kasya cin mitraṃ na kaś cit kasya cit suhṛt arthair arthā nibadhyante gajair vanagajā iva
english: No one is anyone's friend, no one anyone's well-wisher; interests are bound to interests as wild elephants are bound by tame elephants.

sanskrit: na hi kaś cit kṛte kārye kartāraṃ samavekṣate tasmāt sarvāṇi kāryāṇi sāvaśeṣāṇi kārayet
english: For once a task is done, no one regards the doer of it; therefore one should have all one's tasks carried out with something still left undone.

sanskrit: tasmin kāle 'pi ca bhavān divākīrtibhayānvitaḥ mama na grahaṇe śaktaḥ palāyanaparāyaṇaḥ
english: And even at that moment you, gripped by terror of the outcast, will be intent on flight and unable to seize me.

sanskrit: chinnaṃ tu tantubāhulyaṃ tantur eko 'vaśeṣitaḥ chetsyāmy ahaṃ tad apy āśu nirvṛto bhava lomaśa
english: The mass of strands is cut through; one strand alone remains. That too I shall cut at once—be at ease, O shaggy one.

sanskrit: tayoḥ saṃvadator evaṃ tathaivāpannayor dvayoḥ kṣayaṃ jagāma sā rātrir lomaśaṃ cāviśad bhayam
english: As the two of them conversed thus, each still caught in his plight, the night wore to its close, and fear came over the shaggy one.

sanskrit: tataḥ prabhātasamaye vikṛtaḥ kṛṣṇapiṅgalaḥ sthūlasphig vikaco rūkṣaḥ śvacakraparivāritaḥ
english: Then, as dawn came on, there appeared a misshapen man, dark-tawny, broad of haunch, wild-haired and harsh, ringed about by a pack of dogs—

sanskrit: śaṅkukarṇo mahāvaktraḥ palito ghoradarśanaḥ parigho nāma caṇḍālaḥ śastrapāṇir adṛśyata
english: spike-eared, huge-mouthed, grizzled, fearful to look upon, an outcast named Parigha, weapon in hand, came into view.

sanskrit: taṃ dṛṣṭvā yamadūtābhaṃ mārjāras trastacetanaḥ uvāca palitaṃ bhītaḥ kim idānīṃ kariṣyasi
english: Seeing him, like a messenger of Yama, the cat, his wits unstrung with terror, said in fear to the grey one: "What will you do now?"

sanskrit: atha cāpi susaṃtrastau taṃ dṛṣṭvā ghoradarśanam kṣaṇena nakulolūkau nairāśyaṃ jagmatus tadā
english: And the mongoose and the owl too, sorely frightened at the sight of that terrible figure, in an instant gave up all hope.

sanskrit: balinau matimantau ca saṃghātaṃ cāpy upāgatau aśakyau sunayāt tasmāt saṃpradharṣayituṃ balāt
english: Strong and clever, and now allied together, the two—because of the mouse's good policy—could not be overpowered by force.

sanskrit: kāryārthaṃ kṛtasaṃdhī tau dṛṣṭvā mārjāramūṣakau ulūkanakulau tūrṇaṃ jagmatuḥ svaṃ svam ālayam
english: Seeing the cat and mouse, who had made their pact for a purpose, the owl and the mongoose hastened off, each to his own dwelling.

sanskrit: tataś ciccheda taṃ tantuṃ mārjārasya sa mūṣakaḥ vipramukto 'tha mārjāras tam evābhyapatad drumam
english: Then the mouse cut through that last strand of the cat's, and the cat, set free, sprang up that very tree.

sanskrit: sa ca tasmād bhayān mukto mukto ghoreṇa śatruṇā bilaṃ viveśa palitaḥ śākhāṃ bheje ca lomaśaḥ
english: And the grey one, released from that danger and from his dreaded foe, entered his burrow, while the shaggy cat took to a branch.

sanskrit: unmātham apy athādāya caṇḍālo vīkṣya sarvaśaḥ vihatāśaḥ kṣaṇenātha tasmād deśād apākramat jagāma ca svabhavanaṃ caṇḍālo bharatarṣabha
english: The outcast, taking up his trap and looking all about, his hopes ruined, in a moment withdrew from that place and went home, O bull of the Bharatas.

sanskrit: tatas tasmād bhayān mukto durlabhaṃ prāpya jīvitam bilasthaṃ pādapāgrasthaḥ palitaṃ lomaśo 'bravīt
english: Then, released from that danger and his hard-won life regained, the shaggy one, perched at the treetop, spoke to the grey one in his burrow:

sanskrit: akṛtvā saṃvidaṃ kāṃ cit sahasāham upaplutaḥ kṛtajñaṃ kṛtakalyāṇaṃ kaccin māṃ nābhiśaṅkase
english: "Without making any agreement, I came to you suddenly in my distress. Grateful as I am, and after the good I have done you—surely you do not now distrust me?

sanskrit: gatvā ca mama viśvāsaṃ dattvā ca mama jīvitam mitropabhogasamaye kiṃ tvaṃ naivopasarpasi
english: Having won my trust and granted me my life, why is it that, now the time has come to enjoy a friend, you do not come near me?

sanskrit: kṛtvā hi pūrvaṃ mitrāṇi yaḥ paścān nānutiṣṭhati na sa mitrāṇi labhate kṛcchrāsv āpatsu durmatiḥ
english: He who first makes friends but afterward does not keep faith with them—that fool wins no friends in times of hardship and calamity.

sanskrit: tat kṛto 'haṃ tvayā mitraṃ sāmarthyād ātmanaḥ sakhe sa māṃ mitratvam āpannam upabhoktuṃ tvam arhasi
english: Now I have been made your friend by your own power, comrade; having gained me as a friend, you ought to enjoy my fellowship.

sanskrit: yāni me santi mitrāṇi ye ca me santi bāndhavāḥ sarve tvāṃ pūjayiṣyanti śiṣyā gurum iva priyam
english: All the friends I have and all my kinsmen will honor you, as pupils honor a beloved teacher.

sanskrit: ahaṃ ca pūjayiṣye tvāṃ samitragaṇabāndhavam jīvitasya pradātāraṃ kṛtajñaḥ ko na pūjayet
english: And I myself will honor you, together with all your band of friends and kin. What grateful soul would not honor the giver of his life?

sanskrit: īśvaro me bhavān astu śarīrasya gṛhasya ca arthānāṃ caiva sarveṣām anuśāstā ca me bhava
english: Be the lord over me, over my body and my house and all my goods; be my guide and director.

sanskrit: amātyo me bhava prājña piteva hi praśādhi mām na te 'sti bhayam asmatto jīvitenātmanaḥ śape
english: Be my counselor, O wise one, and rule me as a father does; you have no cause to fear me—by my own life I swear it."

sanskrit: buddhyā tvam uśanāḥ sākṣād bale tv adhikṛtā vayam tvanmantrabalayukto hi vindeta jayam eva ha
english: "In intellect you are Uśanas himself; in strength, it is we who hold command. Endowed with your counsel and our might, one would surely win victory."

sanskrit: evam uktaḥ paraṃ sāntvaṃ mārjāreṇa sa mūṣakaḥ uvāca paramārthajñaḥ ślakṣṇam ātmahitaṃ vacaḥ
english: Thus soothed with the utmost conciliation by the cat, the mouse, who knew where his true good lay, spoke smooth words serving his own welfare:

sanskrit: yad bhavān āha tat sarvaṃ mayā te lomaśa śrutam mamāpi tāvad bruvataḥ śṛṇu yat pratibhāti mām
english: "All that you have said I have heard, O shaggy one; now hear me too as I speak, and what seems true to me.

sanskrit: veditavyāni mitrāṇi boddhavyāś cāpi śatravaḥ etat susūkṣmaṃ loke 'smin dṛśyate prājñasaṃmatam
english: Friends must be discerned, and enemies likewise understood. This is seen to be a most subtle matter in this world, one the wise hold in regard.

sanskrit: śatrurūpāś ca suhṛdo mitrarūpāś ca śatravaḥ sāntvitās te na budhyante rāgalobhavaśaṃ gatāḥ
english: There are well-wishers in the guise of foes, and foes in the guise of friends; men beguiled by their soothing do not see through them, fallen under the sway of passion and greed.

sanskrit: nāsti jātyā ripur nāma mitraṃ nāma na vidyate sāmarthyayogāj jāyante mitrāṇi ripavas tathā
english: There is no such thing as an enemy by birth, nor any friend by birth; it is through the workings of interest that friends are made, and foes as well.

sanskrit: yo yasmiñ jīvati svārthaṃ paśyet tāvat sa jīvati sa tasya tāvan mitraṃ syād yāvan na syād viparyayaḥ
english: As long as a man sees his own advantage in another's living, so long does that other thrive; and so long is he that man's friend—until the reverse becomes true.

sanskrit: nāsti maitrī sthirā nāma na ca dhruvam asauhṛdam arthayuktyā hi jāyante mitrāṇi ripavas tathā
english: There is no such thing as a stable friendship, nor any fixed enmity; for it is by the working of interest that friends arise, and foes likewise.

sanskrit: mitraṃ ca śatrutām eti kasmiṃś cit kālaparyaye śatruś ca mitratām eti svārtho hi balavattaraḥ
english: A friend turns to an enemy in some turn of time, and an enemy turns to a friend; for self-interest is the stronger force.

sanskrit: yo viśvasati mitreṣu na cāśvasati śatruṣu arthayuktim avijñāya calitaṃ tasya jīvitam
english: He who trusts in friends and does not trust in foes, not understanding how interest works—his life is unsteady.

sanskrit: arthayuktim avijñāya yaḥ śubhe kurute matim mitre vā yadi vā śatrau tasyāpi calitā matiḥ
english: He who, not understanding how interest works, sets his mind on what seems fair—whether in a friend or in a foe—his judgment too is unsteady.

sanskrit: na viśvased aviśvaste viśvaste 'pi na viśvaset viśvāsād bhayam utpannaṃ mūlāny api nikṛntati
english: One should not trust the untrustworthy, nor even the trustworthy trust too far; danger born of misplaced trust cuts away one's very roots.

sanskrit: arthayuktyā hi dṛśyante pitā mātā sutās tathā mātulā bhāgineyāś ca tathā saṃbandhibāndhavāḥ
english: For it is through the working of interest that one finds a father, a mother, sons, maternal uncles, nephews, and kindred and relations alike.

sanskrit: putraṃ hi mātāpitaru tyajataḥ patitaṃ priyam loko rakṣati cātmānaṃ paśya svārthasya sāratām
english: Mother and father will forsake even a beloved son who has fallen, and the world looks after its own self—behold the sovereignty of self-interest.

sanskrit: taṃ manye nikṛtiprajñaṃ yo mokṣaṃ pratyanantaram kṛtyaṃ mṛgayase kartuṃ sukhopāyam asaṃśayam
english: I hold him to be of a treacherous mind who, the very instant after his release, seeks to do a deed by easy means—of this there is no doubt.

sanskrit: asmin nilaya eva tvaṃ nyagrodhād avatāritaḥ pūrvaṃ niviṣṭam unmāthaṃ capalatvān na buddhavān
english: Brought down to this very dwelling-place from the banyan, you, in your rashness, did not notice the trap set out before you.

sanskrit: ātmanaś capalo nāsti kuto 'nyeṣāṃ bhaviṣyati tasmāt sarvāṇi kāryāṇi capalo hanty asaṃśayam
english: A reckless one is no good even to himself—how then could he be to others? Therefore the reckless man ruins all his undertakings, beyond doubt.

sanskrit: bravīti madhuraṃ kaṃ cit priyo me ha bhavān iti tan mithyākaraṇaṃ sarvaṃ vistareṇāpi me śṛṇu
english: You say something sweet—"You are dear to me here." That is all a making of falsehood; hear me out upon it in full.

sanskrit: kāraṇāt priyatām eti dveṣyo bhavati kāraṇāt arthārthī jīvaloko 'yaṃ na kaś cit kasya cit priyaḥ
english: From a cause one becomes dear; from a cause one becomes hateful. This world of the living seeks its own gain; no one is dear to anyone.

sanskrit: sakhyaṃ sodarayor bhrātror daṃpatyor vā parasparam kasya cin nābhijānāmi prītiṃ niṣkāraṇām iha
english: The fellowship of brothers born of one womb, or of husband and wife with each other—nowhere here do I recognize any affection without a cause.

sanskrit: yady api bhrātaraḥ kruddhā bhāryā vā kāraṇāntare svabhāvatas te prīyante netaraḥ prīyate janaḥ
english: Even if brothers grow angry, or a wife, in some other matter, they hold affection by their very nature; no other person holds it so.

sanskrit: priyo bhavati dānena priyavādena cāparaḥ mantrahomajapair anyaḥ kāryārthaṃ prīyate janaḥ
english: One man becomes dear by gifts, another by pleasant speech, another by spells, oblations, and muttered prayers; man holds affection for the sake of his own ends.

sanskrit: utpanne kāraṇe prītir nāsti nau kāraṇāntare pradhvaste kāraṇasthāne sā prītir vinivartate
english: Affection between us arose when a cause arose; in some other matter there is none, and when the ground of that cause is destroyed, that affection turns away.

sanskrit: kiṃ nu tat kāraṇaṃ manye yenāhaṃ bhavataḥ priyaḥ anyatrābhyavahārārthāt tatrāpi ca budhā vayam
english: What cause, then, can I suppose makes me dear to you—other than as something to be eaten? And of that too I am well aware.

sanskrit: kālo hetuṃ vikurute svārthas tam anuvartate svārthaṃ prājño 'bhijānāti prājñaṃ loko 'nuvartate
english: Time fashions the occasion, and self-interest follows after it; the wise man discerns his own interest, and the world follows the wise.

sanskrit: na tv īdṛśaṃ tvayā vācyaṃ viduṣi svārthapaṇḍite akāle 'viṣamasthasya svārthahetur ayaṃ tava
english: But you should not speak in this fashion to one who knows, one learned in his own interest. Out of season and standing in no peril, this talk of yours is only for your own ends.

sanskrit: tasmān nāhaṃ cale svārthāt susthitaḥ saṃdhivigrahe abhrāṇām iva rūpāṇi vikurvanti kṣaṇe kṣaṇe
english: Therefore I shall not stray from my own interest, standing firm in the matter of peace and war; for like the shapes of clouds, alliances alter from moment to moment.

sanskrit: adyaiva hi ripur bhūtvā punar adyaiva sauhṛdam punaś ca ripur adyaiva yuktīnāṃ paśya cāpalam
english: This very day an enemy, then this very day a friend, and again this very day an enemy—behold the fickleness of expedients.

sanskrit: āsīt tāvat tu maitrī nau yāvad dhetur abhūt purā sā gatā saha tenaiva kālayuktena hetunā
english: There was friendship between us only so long as the cause existed before; it has departed together with that very cause, which was bound to the moment.

sanskrit: tvaṃ hi me 'tyantataḥ śatruḥ sāmarthyān mitratāṃ gataḥ tat kṛtyam abhinirvṛttaṃ prakṛtiḥ śatrutāṃ gatā
english: For you are utterly my enemy, who by force of circumstance became my friend. That business is now accomplished, and your nature has returned to enmity.

sanskrit: so 'ham evaṃ praṇītāni jñātvā śāstrāṇi tattvataḥ praviśeyaṃ kathaṃ pāśaṃ tvatkṛtaṃ tad vadasva me
english: Knowing as I do, in their truth, the treatises laid down in this wise—how should I enter a snare of your making? Tell me that.

sanskrit: tvadvīryeṇa vimukto 'haṃ madvīryeṇa tathā bhavān anyonyānugrahe vṛtte nāsti bhūyaḥ samāgamaḥ
english: By your strength I was set free, and by my strength were you; the mutual favor being now rendered, there is no further coming together.

sanskrit: tvaṃ hi saumya kṛtārtho 'dya nirvṛttārthās tathā vayam na te 'sty anyan mayā kṛtyaṃ kiṃ cid anyatra bhakṣaṇāt
english: For you, good friend, have today gained your end, and we too have accomplished ours; you have no further use for me—save to make a meal of me.

sanskrit: aham annaṃ bhavān bhoktā durbalo 'haṃ bhavān balī nāvayor vidyate saṃdhir niyukte viṣame bale
english: I am the food and you the eater; I am weak and you are strong. No pact can hold between us two, since our strengths are so unequal.

sanskrit: saṃmanye 'haṃ tava prajñāṃ yan mokṣāt pratyanantaram bhakṣyaṃ mṛgayase nūnaṃ sukhopāyam asaṃśayam
english: I take the measure of your wisdom: that the very instant after your release you are surely seeking your prey by easy means—of this there is no doubt."
